title: Flexbox Layout Mechanics
description: Master 1-dimensional CSS layouts: main and cross axis alignment, justify-content, align-items, flex-direction, and flexible wrapping.

objectives.statement: Identify how flex-direction establishes main vs cross axes.
Apply justify-content and align-items to center and distribute child elements.

content.title: Mastering Flexible Box Layout
content.hook: Centering an element vertically and horizontally used to require hacky CSS. Flexbox solved this once and for all with two directional axes.
content.context: Flexbox provides dynamic space distribution and alignment across screens of any size.
goals: Understand how the main axis changes when flex-direction is row vs column.
Write CSS rules to center and space items in navigation bars and cards.

content.title: The Two Axes of Flexbox
content.text: When you apply display: flex to a container, it creates a flex formatting context. The main axis is determined by flex-direction (row by default). justify-content always controls alignment along the main axis. align-items always controls alignment along the perpendicular cross axis.

callout.text: If flex-direction is set to 'column', justify-content controls vertical alignment and align-items controls horizontal alignment!

content.keyTakeaway: justify-content aligns along the main axis; align-items aligns along the cross axis.

content.title: Build a Centered Hero Card
content.prompt: Update the .container class to use Flexbox, center all children horizontally and vertically, and add a 16px gap between items.

feedback.correct: Great job! display: flex with justify-content: center and align-items: center perfectly centers children.
feedback.incorrect: Make sure you include display: flex, justify-content: center, align-items: center, and gap: 16px in the .container selector.

content.prompt: Order the steps of the browser layout engine when resolving Flexbox rules for a container.

items.text: 1. Establish flex formatting context on parent (display: flex)
2. Determine main axis direction from flex-direction (row/column)
4. Distribute available free space along main axis (justify-content)

content.explanation: Flex container formatting establishes direction first, calculates sizes, distributes space, and finally aligns across the cross axis.

feedback.correct: Spot on! That accurately mirrors browser layout flow.
feedback.incorrect: Review the order: formatting context -> direction -> size calculation -> space distribution -> cross alignment.

content.prompt: Where will items inside .nav-bar be distributed along the page?
options: Horizontally across the top of the container
Vertically from top to bottom with equal space between them
Stacked on top of each other at the top edge with no space
content.explanation: Because flex-direction is column, the main axis is vertical (height: 300px). justify-content: space-between distributes items vertically from top to bottom.

validation.expected: Vertically from top to bottom with equal space between them

feedback.correct: Correct! Column direction turns the vertical axis into the main axis.
feedback.incorrect: Remember: flex-direction: column makes the vertical axis the main axis governed by justify-content.

content.prompt: Explain why knowing the difference between the main axis and cross axis prevents layout confusion when using flex-direction: column.
guidelines: Describe how container height affects column distribution.
content.sampleResponse: When flex-direction changes to column, justify-content operates vertically along container height, and align-items operates horizontally across container width.
